title: Network and control theory for difficult-to-treat mood and anxiety disorders (NECTAR)
summary:
Although intensive scientific approaches already have been made, it remains unclear, which factors determine the effectiveness of psychotherapy. 
Nevertheless, in the last few years, two basic principles were defined as requirements for successful processes of change in the psychotherapeutic sessions: the orientation on scientific guidelines for the respective psychological disorder and the adjustment of therapeutic interventions to the individual needs of patients (personalization). It's still not scientifically proven, which patient benefits of the guideline-oriented, and which of the personalized psychotherapeutic treatment. 
This study aims to evaluate which factors have the most influence on the effectiveness of cognitive behavior therapy, if this is either aligned to therapeutic guidelines or to the principle of personalization.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
main diagnosis of depressive or anxiety disorder (ICD-11)
at least two guideline-oriented psychotherapeutic and/or pharmacologic treatments in the past (also if psychotherapy was combined with pharmacotherapy)
- comorbidities are approved 
- sufficient german language skills 
- covered by a german statutory medical health insurance
Exclusion criteria:
Currently receiving ongoing psychotherapeutic treatment,
acute suicidality, suicide attempt within the past three months, 
current alcohol/ substance dependence, 
primary diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder,
lifetime diagnosis of Bipolar I disorder, current or past psychotic disorder, diagnosis of emotionally unstable personality disorder of borderline type, 
organic brain disorders,
change in psychotropic medication within four weeks prior to study participation, serious medical conditions preventing participation in psychotherapy, psychiatric conditions requiring treatment in an alternative setting (e.g., BMI < 16.5).
